title: Sharpening transfers saturated towers and functorial desingularization rules
statement:
Let $M$ be a fine torsion-free monoscheme with finite affine cover [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization]. Assume additionally that its sharpening $M^\sharp$ is torsion free in the sense of [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]: every sharp stalk has torsion-free group completion. Image under $\lambda:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M/\mathcal M^\times$ bijects coherent ideals on $M$ with coherent ideals on $M^\sharp$. Sharpening identifies corresponding saturated blowups, and hence finite ordered saturated blowup towers, preserving nonempty centers, unit-ideal stages, smoothness of the final object, and recursive pullback along smooth maps between such monoschemes. It preserves the contraction convention of [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup], which retains a nonidentity initial saturation even when its ideal is the whole sheaf.

Sharpening induces a natural bijection between smooth-functorial saturated desingularization rules on the full category of these monoschemes (fine, with finite affine cover, and with both ordinary and sharp stalk group completions torsion free) and such rules on all fine torsion-free fans with finite affine covers. Both rules are functorial by contracted pullback with their ideal centers and order. The bijection preserves identity and composition compatibility. It is defined locally even for fans with no global monoscheme lift: lift affine fans to the monoschemes of their sharp monoids and glue the uncontracted restrictions of the rule on the finite disjoint union of these lifts. The resulting fan tower is finite and independent of the affine cover.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-sharpening-blowup-chart-comparison] to $M$: image and inverse image of ideals give the required correspondence, and its glued fraction-chart comparison gives the unique ordered lift of every tower and its recursive pullbacks. By [lem-trf-smooth-tower-index-synchronization], final smoothness and exactly the same contracted indices are preserved, including a nonidentity initial saturation. This proves all assertions about individual objects and towers.

For a fan rule $Q$, define $L(Q)(M)$ as the unique tower lifting $Q(M^\sharp)$ by [lem-trf-sharpening-blowup-chart-comparison]. Its last object is smooth by [lem-trf-smooth-tower-index-synchronization]. For a smooth monoscheme map its sharpening is smooth by that same lemma, so lift the given comparison of $Q$. Compatibility with recursive pullback and contraction identifies this comparison with the required contracted pullback. Uniqueness of ideal lifts and the prescribed fraction maps lift the identity and composition laws as well.

For a monoscheme rule $R$, [lem-trf-affine-lift-tower-descent] glues the uncontracted restrictions of $R$ on the finite disjoint union of sharp affine lifts to a finite contracted fan resolution, without assuming a global lift. By [lem-trf-fan-descent-refinement-pullback] these towers are independent of the cover and affine lifts, and the comparisons along smooth maps preserve centers, order, identities and composition. They therefore define a fan rule $S(R)$.

Finally $S(L(Q))=Q$: on the disjoint union of sharp affine models, lifting and sharpening recover $Q$ by [lem-trf-sharpening-blowup-chart-comparison]; its smooth-surjective cover pullback retains every global index by [lem-trf-smooth-tower-index-synchronization], so gluing recovers $Q(F)$. Conversely cover $M$ by affine monoschemes. By [lem-trf-fine-monoid-unit-splitting], each chart is a smooth surjective lift of its sharp model. Their disjoint union maps are smooth surjections; [lem-trf-smooth-tower-index-synchronization] identifies $R$ there with the lifted towers defining $L(S(R))(M)$. By the descent and refinement comparisons of Step 3 their centers agree on this cover and hence globally at every level. Uniqueness in [lem-trf-sharpening-blowup-chart-comparison] identifies the ordered towers. Thus $L(S(R))=R$; Steps 2--3 preserve the identity and composition comparisons, yielding the asserted natural bijection.
